clue.text: Honour given to capital writer …

parts.note: in card games the jack is one of the honour cards
London is the capital of England

explanation.surface: A distinguished author receives an award, with the thought running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots tie this clue to 9 across, which begins with the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was the American novelist who wrote The Call of the Wild.

clue.text: Lacking any standards, left bouquet upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the joined pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its aroma

explanation.surface: Careless of etiquette, someone has left a bunch of flowers inverted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without moral principles has no ethical code at all.

clue.text: Very involved in maintenance work, so to speak

definitions.text: Very involved in maintenance work, so to speak

parts.words: Very involved in maintenance work, so to speak
parts.note: the phrase for being deeply engaged pictures a repair worker kneeling or wading up to the joints of the legs

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly absorbed in repair jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being immersed up to the leg joints is an idiom for being deeply engaged in something.

clue.text: Unfrocked monk is not working

explanation.surface: A defrocked friar finds himself unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a monk thrown out has left his religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk expelled has left his religious community; a broken machine is idiomatically said to be this.

clue.text: No Italian coppers turned up, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the pieces read upwards as one run

parts.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes police

explanation.surface: No Italian police officers showed up, so to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's style of enunciation and choice of words.

clue.text: Girl enshrined by Colonel Lovelace

indicators.note: something enshrined is held inside, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: A young woman revered by a military officer named Lovelace.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell is a short form of the female name Eleanor or Helen.

clue.text: Have a political bias — keep on striking

explanation.surface: A union member with left-wing loyalties continues the industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BE LABOUR, it means to support Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting the Labour Party is a political leaning; to belabour is to beat repeatedly.

clue.text: Cold meal prison cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the food has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unappetising dinner prepared in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfriendly, detached manner is described as cold.

clue.text: . honour 'e's right to return

parts.note: the dropped-aitch form of he's, taken as its written letters with the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: returning means the synonym for right is read backwards

parts.note: meet is an old word for right or proper

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a Cockney says a man is entitled to his reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e's is the Cockney he's with the aitch dropped; 'to return' turns the word for right backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is a synonym of honouring them.

clue.text: Most dice are tossed in the home

indicators.note: dice that are tossed are thrown about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Most rolls of the dice happen in a family game at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes household matters, things kept within the family dwelling.

clue.text: Allow to desert, in general

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the word for desert inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A permission given for a soldier to go absent in general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to permit or endure it.

clue.text: Sad little boy

explanation.surface: A melancholy small child.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Boy Blue is a figure from an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is a colloquial synonym for sad; the nursery rhyme boy is named Little Boy Blue.

clue.text: A flower to keep one talking

explanation.surface: A bloom worn while detaining someone in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower worn in the lapel has this name; to accost and detain someone in talk is the verb sense.

clue.text: Nails here ready

explanation.surface: A carpenter's nails laid out and prepared for use.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: toenails are found at the ends of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toenails grow on the digits of the feet, and being alert and prepared is an idiom for this phrase.

clue.text: Simple way to achieve financial security

parts.note: easy means simple
a street is a road or way

explanation.surface: An uncomplicated route to becoming comfortably off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this metaphorical road means living in comfort and affluence.

clue.text: Ray distressed poor Ted

indicators.note: something distressed is knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ray is upset about unfortunate Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name beside Ted; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The torpedo is an electric ray, a flat fish that can stun prey.

clue.text: Advance payment for old servant

explanation.surface: Paying ahead for a long-serving domestic.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee paid ahead to secure services, and a household attendant kept on for years.

clue.text: Hopin' for a remedy

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: With its final g dropped, aspiring (hoping) is written aspirin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring means hoping, here clipped informally; the painkiller tablet is a common medicine.

clue.text: A swindler, I am after old gold

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
post is Latin for after
or is the heraldic word for gold, an old usage

explanation.surface: A con artist confesses to chasing antique treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pretending to be another person to deceive is a fraud.

clue.text: Bloomer appearing in a misspelt notice

indicators.note: a misspelt word has its letters wrong, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blunder shows up in a badly written announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood, is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Where the 'Hesperus' went and broke

explanation.surface: A shipwreck that also wrecked someone's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wreck of the Hesperus is a Longfellow poem in which the schooner is dashed on a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship ended up wrecked on a reef; being penniless or a marriage failing is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: When speaking he's become boring

indicators.note: speaking signals the man's name is said out loud to give a word with another spelling

parts.note: the man is the apostle Paul, the name Saul took after his conversion

explanation.surface: A man who has turned dull whenever he talks.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUL and PALL sound alike; to pall is to lose appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: When something palls it grows tedious and loses its interest.

clue.text: Look bright without ultimately having to pay attention

indicators.note: without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: to glisten is to shine or look bright

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Appear cheerful without having to concentrate in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The G at the end of 'having' is removed from GLISTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed what is said is to give it one's ear.

clue.text: Increase his lead to 23-5, giving away penultimate point

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter
giving away means losing, and penultimate fixes which E goes: the one before last

parts.note: twenty-three minus five comes to eighteen
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A sports report: his team pulls ahead to a score of 23-5, though a point is conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: The score 23-5 is read as a subtraction, giving a number; 'giving away penultimate' removes the E before last.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten something is to raise or intensify it.

clue.text: Plays that offer you some original characters

indicators.note: the original characters of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Theatre productions that give the audience some striking roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a noun for dramas; it is a verb, as a child plays.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly.

clue.text: Study it outside — it has unknown individual characteristics

indicators.note: outside puts the first it around the study word

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a private study room
taken as written
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: Examine it from the exterior to discover what makes a person unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfhood is made up of the distinctive traits that mark someone out.

clue.text: On the way back, go off course to fish, and drift

indicators.note: the way back means both pieces are read from right to left as one run

parts.note: a ship that yaws swings off its heading
the eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A boat returning home wanders off course to go fishing and drifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way back' turns YAWEEL into LEEWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is the sideways drift of a vessel blown downwind.

clue.text: Embarrassed, grew silent and hot

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A blushing person falls quiet and feels the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweltering describes oppressive, uncomfortable heat.
